Lore-and-Setting/International-Governmen.title: International Government
Lore-and-Setting/International-Governmen.content:
The International Government is primarily a pact between most of the world’s individual governments to help ensure aid, safety and basic resources for all humans are provided. This includes running the International School.
Once they found out about the Lead Researcher and his plans with the Chromatic Organization they signed a secrecy agreement for the organization in return for various agreements.

The Chromatics don’t kill/harm government employees/members/buildings/proceedings
Nobody without morally questionable large scale intentions/actions (pretty much all Civilians) should be harmed
The government should be able to assign contracts to the Chromatics
The government does not sabotage any attempts that the Chromatics make to complete their missions correctly

Lore-and-Setting/Mercenaries.title: Mercenaries
Lore-and-Setting/Mercenaries.content: Mercenaries are people in the Chromatic universe whose goals include killing or fighting against Chromatics. The term “Mercenary” is pretty general, and it extends beyond people who would be considered regular mercenaries.

Lore-and-Setting/Setting.title: Setting
Lore-and-Setting/Setting.content:
This universe takes place in an almost completely monochromatic universe, sometime around the 26th century. This universe is very closely based on the real world, though the primary difference between the real world and this universe is that evolution and various developments are all centered on the world being monochromatic.
All civilians are subject to both their local governments and the International Government.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Agency
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
The Chromatic agencies are small sections of the Chromatic Organization that act as their own branch, and each agency competes with the others in order to receive the best organization evaluations. Higher evaluations net better perks for the Chromatics under that agency, and Chromatics are encouraged to both complete missions and kill opposing Chromatics in order to boost their agency evaluations.
Each Chromatic agency has multiple stations across the globe to house, aid and brief their Chromatics.
There are 6 agencies, each corresponding to one color.

Red
Blue
Green
Purple
Pink
Orange

Other agency colors do not exist, as each agency is supposed to have distinct colors. Chromatics will also bleed the color of their agency, so additional colors like yellow or brown would make lethal fights with Chromatics look more gross than they need to. These colors are also supposed to have full saturation and value, so only full hues would be considered as possible agency colors.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Blood Encoding
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
Blood encoding is the process of adding computer readable data to the blood cells of a Chromatic.
The main purpose of blood encoding is to provide a way to add unique identification data to a Chromatic that does not involve reading a Chromatic’s DNA. This is then used in tandem with mesh metal blades, which stores liquids that come in contact with its surface.
For example, If a Chromatic wounds and kills an opposing Chromatic with a blade that uses mesh metal, the opposing Chromatic’s blood can then be taken to a weapon rinsing site to read its encoded data and reward the winning Chromatic depending on the Class rank stored in the encoded blood.
Any changes to a single encoded blood cell’s data will modify any surrounding encoded blood cells near instantaneously, as long as that blood cell is inside of that Chromatic’s body. Once an encoded blood cell leaves a Chromatic’s body, it cannot be modified any further.
Below are the types of tracked data that encoded blood stores.

The Chromatic’s identification number (which can then be used to look up their Agency and Class rank)
The Chromatic’s Consciousness (Conscious, Unconscious)
The Chromatic’s Vitality (Alive, Dead)
The identification number of any mesh metal blade that comes in contact with the cell (for tracking which opposing Chromatics damaged the receiving Chromatic, see Class credits)

Roughly 1/5th of a Chromatic’s blood is encoded, and any lost blood through their body’s internal regulations or wounds are replaced upon visiting a healing table.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Chromatic Mentorships
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
If a Chromatics wishes to obtain training before taking on missions, they can seek a mentorship to train with an experienced Chromatic. A Chromatic can apply for a mentorship as soon as they become a Chromatic, and a Chromatic can become a mentor when they reach Class 6.
Chromatics can continue training with the mentor until they or the mentor feel ready for the Chromatic to be left on their own.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Chromatic Station
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
Chromatic Stations essentially act as hubs for the Chromatics, and they provide many services for the Chromatics who go there.
Each station is built underground to stay hidden from the public more easily.
They provide:

Housing/Living spaces
Dining/Food in general
Healing and recovery services
Briefings
Weapon Rinsing
Training
Entertainment and recreation
Transportation to other stations
Small personal storages

Housing/Living
There are various bedrooms and personal spaces that Chromatics can rent out using their Mission credits. These rooms can be occupied with any amount of people at a time, and the rooms generally serve to give private time between any Chromatics who stay in them. Chromatics can also rent the bedrooms if they want to sleep at all. Because of the reduced need for rest due to the Initial Serum taken by all Chromatics, Chromatics usually take some kind of drug that aids with falling asleep, which is provided with the room.
Dining/Food
All Chromatic stations have a dining area/cafeteria where Chromatics can redeem their Mission credits for food (Chromatics aren’t necessarily required to eat in the first place, read Initial Serum for more.) All food is made in the station, usually to order, and each station has a surprising variety of food. Because of their slower metabolism and generally reduced need to eat food due to the Initial Serum taken by all Chromatics, Chromatics usually take a drug to mitigate their body’s reaction to the food being eaten as to not produce too much energy. After eating their food or before going to a mission, Chromatics can then visit a Healing Table to clear their body of the drug and any remaining food in their body.
Healing/Recovery services
This is mostly relegated to the Healing Tables and the professionals who run them.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Chromatics
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
Chromatics are highly skilled assassins that complete contracts. Once someone is qualified to become a Chromatic, they are injected with a Serum that provides them with stronger athletic capabilities. The same serum also transforms the Chromatic’s blood to take on the color of their agency. Features like their hair and irises also take on the color, distinguishing themselves from non-Chromatics.
All Chromatics must have a type of face covering (like a mask, visor, etc.), though it’s only because it looks cool, and not for any stealthy/identity reasons.
Chromatics are assigned to their own Agency, which determines which color their design is based on. They are also given a Class Rank that indicates their experience as a Chromatic. Gaining a higher Class requires a Chromatic to kill other Chromatics from opposing agencies to prove their combat expertise.
In order to confirm missions and opposing Chromatic kills, Chromatics also wield bladed weapons made with a synthesized metal specifically designed to keep track of whatever blood touches its surface. That blood can later be traced back to whoever was injured/killed with it, and the Chromatic can then be attributed with their appropriate payouts.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Class 10
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
Rather than being a direct continuation of the 9th Class rank, Class 10 acts more as a coveted position across every Chromatic. Only one Chromatic amongst the entire Chromatic Organization may be awarded the Class 10 rank at a time. Once a Class 10 is killed by another Chromatic, That Chromatic is awarded with the Class 10 rank.
If a Class 10 Chromatic is killed by something other than an opposing Chromatic, the Chromatic with the highest Class rank and credits amongst all agencies is then awarded the Class 10 rank.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Class
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
Basic Overview
Every Chromatic is ranked amongst other Chromatics via their Class. The Class Rank indicates the Chromatic’s skill in fighting opposing Chromatics, and it is increased via earning credits. All Chromatics start out with a Class rank of Class 1. The highest Class that a Chromatic can reach via credits is Class 9, though exactly one Chromatic at any given time can also have the Class 10 ranking, which is awarded upon killing the current Class 10.
A Chromatic’s current Class is indicated via their Rank Badge.
credits are only rewarded if a Chromatic, using their own weapon, successfully lands the last lethal wound upon an opposing Chromatic. This must be done using the Chromatic’s assigned weapon, since the blood of the opposing Chromatic will be stored in their blade, which is then later used to credit the Chromatic if they rinse their weapon. If that Chromatic was the last person to land a lethal wound upon the opposing Chromatic, and the opposing Chromatic is dead by the time the weapon is rinsed, the surviving Chromatic is then awarded credits.
It should be noted that until a Chromatic’s weapon is rinsed, a Chromatic’s Class will remain the same even if they earn enough credits to qualify for a Class promotion.
The credit requirement to promote to a higher Class is the same as the Chromatic’s current rank. For example, a Class 5 Chromatic will need to acquire 5 credits in order to reach Class 6, and a Class 3 Chromatic would need 3 credits to promote to Class 4, etc.
More Details
The amount of credits awarded per each kill is primarily based on the difference in Class between the two Chromatics. If there is no difference between the two Chromatic’s classes, one credit is awarded. If there is a difference, the awarded credits are multiplied or divided by two for every Class higher or lower than the surviving Chromatic.
In the event that a Chromatic earns more credits than required for a particular rank, the leftover credits are carried over after the promotion.
For example:
A Class 1 kills a Class 2, which earns them 2 credits. After fulfilling the 1 credit requirement to rank up to Class 2, the Chromatic is credited the remaining 1 credit to count towards the new credit requirement. As a result of the initial kill, the Class 1 Chromatic with 0 credits is now a Class 2 Chromatic with 1 credit.
To prevent overwhelming Class rank promotions via higher Class differences, the highest Class that a Chromatic can attain is the Class rank of the highest Class opponent that the Chromatic has ever killed, plus one.
For example, if a Class 1 Chromatic somehow kills three Class 4 Chromatics back to back, and earns 24 credits as a result, that Chromatic cannot rank up past Class 5. After rinsing their weapon, they would be a Class 5 Chromatic with 9 (24-5-4-3-2-1) credits. Any remaining credits will not go towards a promotion until they kill a Chromatic with a Class rank that is at least as high as their own.
A Chromatic can also earn more credits if they kill their opponent without being wounded by their opponent. Successfully doing this will double the base credit count, which will significantly reduce the amount of kills needed to reach the Chromatic’s next promotion.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Healing Table
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
Healing tables are the most prominent and effective way to completely heal a Chromatic of their wounds and ailments. They are only used in Chromatic stations, and use a larger supply of the Healing Serum to cover any injuries that a Chromatic might have.
Healing tables are used in the Medical wing of a Chromatic station, and each table is placed in its own room. Each table can be remotely or physically monitored by the medical staff in the station to ensure that the Chromatic is safely healing.
Each table is large enough to support an 8 foot tall person, and is fitted with equipment that monitors the Chromatic’s wounds, conditions, ailments, infections and fractures, as well as equipment to help with the healing process. This includes mechanical arms that can administer IVs and move the Chromatic’s limbs and clothes on the table, along with sanitation jets to clean the Chromatic off of any blood or environmental dirt, and driers to prepare the Chromatic to leave the table cleanly.
When in use, the table is closed with a glass lid to closely monitor the Chromatic’s oxygen intake.
Here are some very rough models for what a healing table might look like.
Uncovered:

Covered:

The process of using a healing table is as follows.
First, the Chromatic either makes an appointment to reserve a healing table, or enters an available healing table room if they are either entering or returning from the public.
If the Chromatic is wounded, the Chromatic should remove any clothing that directly covers/surrounds their wounds, though if removing the article of clothing would damage/amplify a wound further, the Chromatic can still use the table with the staff manually overseeing more of the table’s procedures. Clothes can also be left to be patched and cleaned by a staff tailor during the time that the Chromatic is on the table.
The Chromatic then lays down onto the table with their back against the table’s surface, and their legs and arms slightly spread out to give room for any remote injections. Once on the table, either the Chromatic or a staff member punctures the user with a needle to administer both the initial Healing Serum and an anesthetic.
From there, the Chromatic will remain unconscious through the rest of their time on the table. Whatever wounds, fractures or infections are present are then sanitized and treated with the healing serum, and any debris lodged in the body is also removed. If the Chromatic previously opted into keeping the scars of their wounds, scars will not be treated. Whatever blood was lost is replaced, with any new blood encoded to the treated Chromatic.
Once the Chromatic is fully healed and is cleaned of any blood and debris, they are no longer provided anesthesia, and are then woken up to collect their belongings and leave the healing table’s room.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Mesh Metal
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
This type of metal is the primary metal used in Chromatic weapons.
This material consists of a strong web of other metals, leaving extremely small gaps for liquids to seep through. The web is made of thin films of other metals, which all have a grid of small hexagonal slits, which lightly overlap onto the slits of other metal films. The material is somehow quite firm and stable, though it is not very malleable, since it would close whatever gaps that were bent fairly easily. Because of this, most shapes need to be cut rather than molded, and sharpening blades that use mesh metal can only be realistically done in Chromatic stations.
Chromatic blades use Mesh Metal to confirm opposing Chromatics kills via storing Chromatic blood and verifying the blood encoding on the stored blood. Mesh metal also interacts with the encoded blood itself, storing values like the amount of force the blade pushes against the blood cell and identification details of both the blade and the Chromatic that inflicted damage upon the receiving Chromatic. The damaged Chromatic’s blood is then stored elsewhere in the weapon after coming in contact with the blade, and it can then be extracted via aweapon rinse to redeem any credit earned from the kill.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Research Lab
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content: This lab researched the Serums, Mesh Metal, Healing Tables, and Blood Encoding technologies that were eventually put in large scale use once the Lead Researcher established an organization for the Chromatic agencies.

Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.title: Serums
Lore-and-Setting/Chromatic-Organization/.content:
These are the serums that Chromatics can use.

Serums
Serums

Serums are made to cater to a specific agency’s color, and serve various purposes for the Chromatics.
Transformation Serum
Transforms the injected person into a Chromatic of a specific agency’s color. Initiates blood encoding, provides higher pain tolerance, higher endurance, heightened senses, significantly slower metabolism, and a reduced need for sleep/rest.
Healing Serum
Regenerates damaged body parts. As the serum flows through the Chromatic’s bloodstream, it seeks the nearest damaged/open wounds and uses its own molecules to generate new cells in place of the damaged/torn cells. This heals wounds entirely, prevents bleeding, and it relieves pain fairly quickly once the damaged cells are regenerated.
This serum does not recreate severed body parts, but the serum does try its best to heal the exposed flesh as cleanly as possible. For example, if the serum entered the bloodstream of an arm that is severed of its hand, it would round off the arm’s stump, generating flesh that covers the wound, and would repair the nearest nerve routes to alleviate any disorientation that comes with not having a hand anymore.
Healing Serum also makes its user feel more exhausted, since the user’s body is tricked into thinking that it is performing the cell generation by itself, and begins to signal signs of tiredness the administered area.
Chromatics are given syringes of the Healing Serum to use on the field, though using them during combat is discouraged due to the tiredness that comes soon after administering the serum.

Lore-and-Setting/Scenarios/Canon-Point.title: Canon Point
Lore-and-Setting/Scenarios/Canon-Point.content: The Canon Point is the single point in time between the “canon” Past Events and the “non-canon” Scenarios. As of now, the rough estimate for when the Canon Point occurs is in the 26th century.

Lore-and-Setting/Scenarios/Scenarios.title: Scenarios
Lore-and-Setting/Scenarios/Scenarios.content:
All Scenarios involving the Chromatics universe occur after the Canon Point, and are not considered “Canon” in terms of any established story. Scenarios may take place any time after the Canon Point, and generally follow along a story that includes a select group of characters. This choice is made from the fact that I am very indecisive when it comes to creating a long term defined plot and story, especially with a cast of characters that are all supposed to kill each other. “When do I kill off this character?” and “Do I have to focus on this character right now?” are both questions that I don’t need to answer, and I can write pretty much anything that lines up with what the characters in the story would do!
This also allows for other people to come up with their own Scenarios pretty freely, because no Scenarios are necessarily “Canon” anyway. The only “canon” restrictions that I follow are defined with the events that happen before the Canon Point. Anyone can make up their own scenarios, and those scenarios will very likely be just as canon as mine.

Chromatic Info:

































Name:Cyn (from Cynthia)Age:26Agency:BlueClass Rank:5Birthday:October 1stPronouns:she/herSexuality:Pansexual
Cyn is a Class 5 Chromatic.
Is teamed up with Dev, Jay and Dusk, though most of her missions involve working with Jay and Dusk.
Personality
Cyn is outgoing, and hold close interactions with the people around her, whether she views them positively or negatively. She is open to accepting promises or favors from other people, but she is also easily swayed into breaking those promises if she is able to follow a more favorable outcome for herself, or if persuaded into doing anything else. She also frequently engages in starting/continuing gossip or drama about the people she holds close relationships with.
Character Backstory
Cyn originally worked in a law firm as a defense attorney. The reason why she became a Chromatic hasn’t been determined yet.
Character Relationships
Dev
Cyn’s boyfriend and occasional teammate. This is the first romantic relationship where Cyn holds a strong sense of emotional connection with her partner, as opposed to her previous infatuous relationships.
Dusk
Cyn’s teammate. Occasionally hangs out with him, and considers him to be a good teammate and a chill person.
Jay
Cyn’s teammate. She is fairly playful towards him outside of missions, and often provides Jay with personal drama that took place both before and during her time as a Chromatic.
Raine
Cyn’s former law firm co-worker. After Raine blackmails Cyn during their time at their law firm, their relationship turns sour, and their relationship gains a mutual hatred when they find out that they are both Chromatics. Cyn often tries to resolve her arguments with Raine by fighting in practice duels, though Raine often ends up beating Cyn in many of their fights.

Characters/Chromatics/Orange-Agency/Dawn.title: Dawn
Characters/Chromatics/Orange-Agency/Dawn.content:
Dawn currently does not have a reference image.
Chromatic Info:

































Name:DawnAge:24Agency:OrangeClass Rank:5Birthday:May 26thPronouns:she/herSexuality:Pansexual
Dawn is a Class 5 Chromatic.
She is often found together with Eve, her identical twin sister, who is also a Chromatic. She typically wears white, in contrast to her sister, who typically wears black.
Personality
Dawn is outgoing, and is typically optimistic about the life around her. While she can be committed to her goals, she is often quick to decide on many of the important choices in her life. She is usually empathetic to others by default, and is open to interact with others when prompted.
Character Backstory
Her backstory hasn’t been formed yet.
Character Relationships
Eve
Dawn’s identical twin sister. They typically perform/partake in many activities together, simultaneously. This typically includes missions, recreational activities, hangouts, though they can be found separated when interacting with characters that have differing perceptions of the twins.
Dawn usually has to convince Eve to do some of Dawn’s more impulsive ideas, teasing her on until Eve either refuses or begrudgingly follows along. Dawn also actively tries to get Eve to be more outgoing and optimistic, though Eve has never seemed to consider any of Dawn’s attempts to get Eve to socialize.
Dusk
Dawn’s older brother. Dawn has looked up to Dusk for as long as she can remember, and misses their time together since she became a Chromatic. She’s particularly scared of being forced to kill Dusk one day, either by him being notorious enough to be a target on a mission she takes, or even the off-chance that he also becomes an opposing Chromatic if he discovers that she and Eve have become Chromatics.
Kade
Dawn’s boyfriend. Their relationship is largely infatuous, with the two treating the relationship as a situationship amidst others. Dawn frequently compliments Kade on his appearance and accomplishments, and she often indirectly teases him in onto doing various favors for her, like lending points or doing tasks on her behalf.

Characters/Chromatics/Orange-Agency/Eve.content:

Chromatic Info:

































Name:EveAge:24Agency:OrangeClass Rank:5Birthday:May 26thPronouns:she/herSexuality:Asexual
Eve is a Class 5 Chromatic.
She is often found together with Dawn, her identical twin sister, who is also a Chromatic. She typically wears black, in contrast to her sister, who typically wears white.
Personality
Eve usually keeps to herself, and is typically pessimistic about the life around her. She thoroughly thinks through her goals, though she is often scared to commit to them once the opportunity comes to act on the goal. She avoids confrontation or interaction with other by default, and it often takes an extended amount of time for her to gain a closer relationship with any given person.
Character Backstory
Her backstory hasn’t been formed yet.
Character Relationships
Dawn
Eve’s identical twin sister. They typically perform/partake in many activities together, simultaneously. This typically includes missions, recreational activities, hangouts, though they can be found separated when interacting with characters that have differing perceptions of the twins.
Eve typically has to argue against Dawn’s plans and ideas, and usually either gives up on listening to dawn, or caves in to satisfy Dawn. Eve doesn’t really get how Dawn can interact with so many other people comfortable, though she has come to understand that it likely makes Dawn happy to know and talk with so many other people.
She often confines her more personal feelings into Dawn, occasionally setting aside time to communicate her feelings, helping Eve express her emotions.
Dusk
Eve’s older brother. Eve holds respect for Dusk, as she felt like he was an example of an honest person that she could rely on when it came to making promises and dealing with various serious situations. Eve misses Dusk dearly, and is worried that Dusk would think badly of her and Dawn if he found out that they have become Chromatics, especially worrying that he may see the conversion as some form of betrayal.
Kade
Eve knows about Kade from Dawn’s relationship with him. Eve senses that Kade’s outward feelings and intentions are disingenuous, which includes his relationship with Dawn, to his self-confident image. She suspects that Kade is trying to take advantage of Dawn to fulfill a materialistic desire for a relationship.

Characters/Chromatics/Orange-Agency/Kade.content:

Chromatic Info:

































Name:Kade (from Keiji)Age:26Agency:OrangeClass Rank:7Birthday:April 13thPronouns:he/himSexuality:Bisexual
Kade is a Class 7 Chromatic.
Personality
Kade’s most prominent personality trait is his concern over his self image. He attempts to get as many people to admire him as possible, typically through performative actions that are meant to exaggerate some positive aspect about him. This typically includes giving gifts to people, flaunting his skills, and trying to interact with as many people as possible to help gauge his perceived popularity.
He also has a goal of romantically attracting as many people as he can, which results in him maintaining multiple concurring relationships through his time as a Chromatic. These relationships are typically treated as monogamous situationships, and he actively avoids showing his relationships in public in order to appear open to more relationships.
Character Backstory
Kade had trouble keeping his financial responsibility through his adulthood, and had turned to taking loans and odd jobs connected to the criminal world in order to keep himself afloat. Once the time to pay back the loans had run dry, and with no way to reliably pay off the loans, Kade began to take even more action in the criminal world, eventually considering the opportunity to become an assassin. With the mounting debt and responsibilities in his life, Kade decided to become a Chromatic to let go of his previous life in order to start fresh.
Character Relationships
Dawn
One of Kade’s girlfriends. His relationship with Dawn is one of Kade’s favorites, and Kade typically hangs out with Dawn soon after either of them arrive back to their station.
Eve

Name:Cole (from Coleman)Age:29Agency:PinkClass Rank:2Birthday:September 15thPronouns:he/theySexuality:Heterosexual
Cole is a Class 2 Pink Chromatic.
Personality
Cole typically doesn’t interact with others in his daily activities, though he’s good at being able to tell if the people around him need assistance, and tries to help out if he is able to. He is somewhat desensitized to violence and extreme emotions as a result of his time as a mercenary, though he holds a high level of sympathy for those who do experience those emotions.
Character Backstory
Cole was involved in a well-known Mercenaries group, and eventually turned into a right-hand man for one of the organization’s leads. After instability broke out across the organization as a result of constant targeting from the Chromatics, Cole quickly became disillusioned with the organization, as slowly started to lose the trust and abilities granted to him by other members of the organization. As a result, he decided to become a Chromatic to help regain a sense of authority over his actions in some other area of the criminal world.
One of Cole’s additional conditions to become a Chromatic included providing the Chromatics with all of the intelligence he had pertaining to his former organization, along with assisting in missions that targeted the organization. Among the missions he currently takes on, he still finds himself encountering the organization regularly, and he continues to fight against their remaining members.
Character Relationships
Claire
Cole has heard of Claire as one of the stronger Chromatics in his station. Cole knows Claire is a controversial figure among other members in the station, and he tries to avoid places where he thinks Claire may be around to prevent any interaction with her.
